clue.text: Old friends taking care of modern miss, including minister

parts.note: care of is abbreviated c/o on envelopes

indicators.note: including means the title for a modern woman wraps around the clergyman

parts.note: Ms is the modern title for a woman, married or not
a padre is a chaplain or minister

explanation.surface: Old friends look after a young woman of today, with a clergyman among them.
explanation.walkthrough: CO (care of) comes first; then MS is opened up by PADRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-derived word for buddies or companions, here old pals.

clue.text: Body in vehicle — something for police to investigate?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a case is a matter under police inquiry

explanation.surface: A body in a car, which the police will surely look into.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcase (or carcass) is a dead body, usually of an animal.

clue.text: Aims of criminal joining Italy's No 1 illegal gang

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape
Italy's No 1 is the country name's first letter

explanation.surface: The plans of a crook teaming up with Italy's top outlaw mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Mafiosi are members of the Mafia, collectively a criminal gang.

clue.text: Non-patriots in revolt — being negative, they are charged

indicators.note: in revolt means the letters rise up and overturn their order

explanation.surface: Unpatriotic rebels are, being negative types, arrested and charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiprotons are antimatter particles carrying a negative electric charge.

clue.text: Reward soldiers fairly

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
quite means fairly or somewhat

explanation.surface: Pay the troops reasonably well.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to repay or return a favour or kindness.

clue.text: Submarine group very hot

parts.note: in a down clue, sub-marine reads as below the sea, so the sea word sits on top
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A flotilla of submarines is extremely hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' splits as sub (under) and marine (sea): the sea word goes first, above the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Searing means scorching, burning hot.

clue.text: Senior officer taking academic stream in philosopher William's place

parts.note: OC stands for Officer Commanding
the Cam is the river flowing through the university town of Cambridge

explanation.surface: A high-ranking officer takes a university river in the home of a medieval thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Occam, of Occam's razor, was named after the Surrey village (also spelt Ockham).
explanation.definitionFit: The village that gave the medieval friar of 'Occam's razor' fame his surname.

clue.text: Plump and old, needing exercise?

parts.note: PT stands for physical training

explanation.surface: Fat and elderly, so in need of a workout?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' is a verb here: to plump for something is to choose it.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump (for) and to choose are verbs of selection.

clue.text: Clown organised teachers — fair target?

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
NUT is the National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: A clown and a teachers' union, at the fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: At a fairground shy, the prize nut is the thing you throw balls at.

clue.text: Small stone housed in French gallery — essential item for visitor

indicators.note: housed in means the small weight unit is lodged within the French word

parts.note: musée is French for museum or gallery
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A little pebble kept in a French museum, something every tourist must view.
explanation.definitionFit: A must-see is an attraction that no tourist should miss.

clue.text: Getting new gear? Sports official has it

parts.note: a ref is a referee

explanation.surface: A referee is issued fresh kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a renovation in which a ship or building is re-equipped.

clue.text: Hills not unusually having bird sounds around

indicators.note: around means the bird noises go round the shuffled word

parts.note: ducks make quacks

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of not are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Hills, rather surprisingly, lack birdsong all around.
explanation.walkthrough: The Quantocks are a range of hills in Somerset, England. 'unusually' rearranges 'not', and 'around' puts the duck noises round that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Quantock Hills form a ridge in the west of England, known as a pair-word range.

clue.text: A party in difficulty

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party gets into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss or trouble, as in 'without further ado'.

clue.text: Trees found by prince in a foreign country

parts.note: Prince Philip, the late husband of Queen Elizabeth II
pines are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: Trees discovered by a prince abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-east Asian island nation, foreign from a British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Rod deceased, having swallowed yellow chemical

parts.note: a perch is an old unit of length, also called a rod

indicators.note: having swallowed means the dead word takes the heraldic colour inside it

parts.note: late means dead
or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: Rod died after drinking something yellow, a poison perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchlorate is a salt of perchloric acid, used in rocket fuel and fireworks.

clue.text: Incident is placed on record — lines of celebration?

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an ode is a poem of praise

explanation.surface: Something is set down in writing, a poem celebrating it.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one event or occurrence in a series.

clue.text: Rubbish blocking entrance — nasty bit of wire?

indicators.note: blocking means the nonsense word sits inside the doorway, stopping it up

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Junk blocking a doorway, perhaps a bit of dangerous wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangling wire or cord used by assassins; garrotte is the commoner spelling.

clue.text: Throw husband out — ancient fellow whose wife has cheated

indicators.note: out means the letter for husband is taken away from the throwing word

parts.note: to chuck is to throw
old means ancient

explanation.surface: Kicking out the husband: the classic aged figure betrayed by his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: CHUCK loses H to leave CUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuckold is a man whose wife is unfaithful to him.

clue.text: Theologian enthralled by church organ in Somerset village

indicators.note: enthralled by means the theologian is held captive inside the organ

parts.note: the ear is an organ of the body
DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A divine is captivated by a church organ in a West Country village.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar is a village in Somerset, England, famous for its cheese and its gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset village that gave its name to the world's most popular cheese.

clue.text: Skipper goes round southern island missing bit of ship's apparatus

indicators.note: goes round means the skipper word encircles the southern letter
missing means the island letter is left out of the skipper word

parts.note: a skipper is a ship's captain

explanation.surface: The skipper sails round a southern island, lacking a piece of shipboard kit.
explanation.walkthrough: CAPTAIN without I gives CAPTAN, which then goes round S.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship used for winding cables.

clue.text: Excellent worker — I'll get stuck in, resisting authority

indicators.note: get stuck in means the first-person letter is pushed into the middle

parts.note: def is slang for excellent, from hip-hop
an ant is a worker insect
I'll gives the letter I, the 'will' being the future tense of the indicator

explanation.surface: A first-rate grafter vows to get to work, while bucking authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Being defiant means openly resisting or challenging those in charge.

clue.text: Disciple following evangelist, a man of many words

indicators.note: following means the disciple comes after the evangelist

parts.note: John is one of the four Gospel writers
a son can be a follower or disciple, as in a son of the church

explanation.surface: A follower comes after a gospel writer, who preached at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 Dictionary of the English Language.

clue.text: Revolutionary member of Eastern religion eating loaf

indicators.note: eating means the believer swallows the bread

parts.note: a Jain is a follower of Jainism, an Indian religion
a cob is a round loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A rebellious follower of an Indian faith eats bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobins were radical revolutionaries in 1790s France.

clue.text: Spiritualists giving phoney answer

parts.note: sham means fake or phoney

explanation.surface: Mediums giving a fake reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamans are spirit healers who act as go-betweens with the spirit world.

clue.text: Simplicity I have found in nature, abandoning old city

indicators.note: found in means the contraction sits within the other word
abandoning means the ancient city is dropped from nature

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: I discover simplicity in nature, away from the ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops the Mesopotamian city from 'nature', leaving NATE; 'found in' places the contraction inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence or artlessness, lack of sophistication.

clue.text: Naughty act of sexpot, seen retrospectively

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters misbehave and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A seductress's improper behaviour, judged after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'from after the deed', applied to laws or judgements made with hindsight.

clue.text: Boxer went down, with time running out

indicators.note: running out means the letter for time is used up and dropped

parts.note: alit means got down or landed

explanation.surface: A fighter hit the canvas as the clock ran down.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion, is a crossword's favourite fighter.

clue.text: Maiden featured in special birthday poem

indicators.note: featured in means the maiden letter appears inside the rearranged word
special suggests the letters are arranged in a special way

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman appears in a poem written for someone's birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' scrambles BIRTHDAY into DITHYRAB, and 'featured in' places M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb is a wild, impassioned hymn or poem, originally to Dionysus.

clue.text: Tree in river, weak top to bottom

indicators.note: top to bottom means the letter at the head of the down entry is moved to its foot

parts.note: the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: A tree in a river, the frail top fallen to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The yew is an evergreen conifer often found in churchyards.

clue.text: Surprise article, something you may get lost in ?

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

parts.words: something you may get lost in
parts.note: a maze is a labyrinth designed to confuse

explanation.surface: An unexpected item: a place where you might go astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze is to astonish, the verb sense of surprise.

clue.text: Little women, never disheartened, about to begin again

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around into a new order
disheartened means the central letter of never is removed

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A nod to the novel Little Women, never downcast, poised for a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes V from NEVER, leaving NEER; 'about' rearranges W and NEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to resume or start afresh, as with an effort or a subscription.

clue.text: State number being brought to head, having taken drug repeatedly

parts.note: ten is a number
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

indicators.note: repeatedly means the drug's letter is taken twice over

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A number brought to a headland, having taken drugs again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty US states.
